record.original_question: In the adversarial contextual bandit setting with context space X, finite action space A = {1, ..., K}, horizon T, and a nested sequence of finite policy classes Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ ΠM, does there exist an algorithm that simultaneously guarantees, for every m ∈ [M], expected regret to class Πm of order O(√(KT(log |Πm| + log m)))? Here regret to Πm means max over π ∈ Πm of E[Σ_t ℓt(at) − Σ_t ℓt(π(xt))].

evidence.quote: Focusing on contextual bandits, a simple reinforcement learning setting, we ask: Can model selection guarantees be achieved in contextual bandit learning, where a learner must balance exploration and exploitation to make decisions online?
Open Problem 1a Design a contextual bandit algorithm that for any sequence Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ΠM ensures max π∈Πm E[ T ∑ t=1 ℓt(at) − T ∑ t=1 ℓt(π(xt))] ≤ O( √KT(log∣Πm∣ + log m)), for all m ∈ [M].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the adversarial contextual bandit problem with the following setup. Let X be a context space and A = {1, 2, ..., K} a finite action set with K ≥ 2. Fix a horizon T ∈ ℕ. A policy is a function π : X → A. Let Π₁ ⊂ Π₂ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Π_M be a nested sequence of finite policy classes (with M ≥ 1).

The protocol proceeds for t = 1, ..., T as follows:
  • The environment selects a context x_t ∈ X and a loss function ℓ_t : A → [0,1] (chosen possibly adversarially, in advance or obliviously).
  • The learner observes x_t, then selects (possibly randomly) an action a_t ∈ A.
  • The learner observes only the bandit feedback ℓ_t(a_t).

For each m ∈ {1, ..., M}, define the regret of the learner with respect to class Π_m by
   R_m(T) := max_{π ∈ Π_m} 𝔼[ Σ_{t=1}^T ℓ_t(a_t) − Σ_{t=1}^T ℓ_t(π(x_t)) ].

Question: Does there exist a learner (a single algorithm with no prior knowledge of m) such that, for every nested sequence Π₁ ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Π_M and every adversarial environment, simultaneously for all m ∈ {1, ..., M},
   R_m(T) ≤ C · √( K T ( log |Π_m| + log m ) ),
for some absolute constant C > 0?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work establishes a Pareto frontier of matching upper and lower bounds for model selection in (general, including adversarial) contextual bandits with nested policy classes, showing that the desired guarantee O(√(KT(log|Π_m| + log m))) simultaneously for all m is unobtainable even in the stochastic regime. An unavoidable trade-off of the form log(|Π_m|)^{1−α} T^α with α ∈ [1/2, 1) is necessary for general policy classes, thereby resolving the open problem in the negative.

status_evidence.title: The Pareto Frontier of model selection for general Contextual Bandits
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the COLT 2020 open problem on model selection for nested policy classes, showing matching upper and lower bounds with an unavoidable trade-off between the complexity term log|Π_m| and the horizon T.
status_evidence.claim: The open problem was answered negatively: the desired O(√(KT log|Π_m|)) simultaneous guarantee is unobtainable, with a Pareto frontier characterizing achievable trade-offs.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Model Selection for Contextual Bandits (COLT 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Posed Open Problem 1a asking whether √(KT(log|Π_m| + log m)) regret can be achieved simultaneously for all m in a nested sequence of policy classes.
status_evidence.claim: This is the original statement of the open problem at COLT 2020.
